The predicted 1990 noise levels inside Hamlin Garland School will be 54dBA and therefore be below the noise standards.
The noise levels produced by the Airport Spur are not high enough to produce hearing damage. The standards set by Occupational Safety Health Act (OSHA) to prevent hearing damage in industry allow an 82 dBA noise exposure (extrapolation from the 
\epsilon
 hour standards) for 24 hours each day. The highest 1990 noise levels produced with abatement by a combination of the Aiprort Spur and existing I-94 produce a noise exposure of 70dDA for only 6 minutes of the peak noise producing hour of the day.
The harmful psychological effects and annoying effects of speech interference caused by noise exposure were considered in establishing the federal noise standards. Since these standards will be adhered to, both the harmful and annoying effects will not exist.
